intro: You are standing at Malabadi Bridge, in Diyarbakır province, built in 1147. This Artuqid bridge spans the Batman river in a single arch of more than 38 metres, among the widest stone spans of the Middle Ages. And hidden in its flanks are chambers where travellers once slept.
history: The bridge was built over the Batman river in 1147 under the Artuqids, and its single arch spans more than thirty-eight metres. Why so wide? The width was a defence against the spring floods that carry snowmelt down the valley. Chambers in its flanks were set aside so that travellers and caravans could spend the night.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the pointed arch and the traveller rooms in its flanks, then look for the reliefs and the stone parapet.
facts: Did you know? The span is wider than the dome of Hagia Sophia, and very few medieval stone arches were ever built at that scale. Its single span passes thirty-eight metres — medieval stone arches of that width can be counted on one hand. And the rooms in the bridge's flanks were built so that travellers could spend a winter night inside the bridge itself.
outro: This brings our journey to Malabadi Bridge to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. The bridge has carried travellers across the river for centuries; may it carry many more after you. Enjoy your visit.
